title: A Painting Without Its Frame
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の例を用いた論説であり、実在の調査・史料・制度・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: An object displayed in an art gallery is encountered under conditions that may be quite different from those in which it was originally used or produced.
sentences.ja: 美術館に展示された物は当初使われたり作られたりした条件とはかなり異なる条件で出会われる。

sentences.en: The lighting, surrounding objects, and information provided on a label can influence the aspects of a work to which visitors pay attention.
sentences.ja: 照明、周囲の物、ラベル情報は訪問者が注意を払う作品の側面に影響し得る。

sentences.en: A painting that appears to be an independent object in a modern exhibition may once have formed part of a much larger arrangement.
sentences.ja: 現代展示で独立した物に見える絵はかつてもっと大きな配置の一部をなしていたかもしれない。

sentences.en: Its original surroundings may therefore provide information that cannot be obtained by examining its surface alone.
sentences.ja: そこで元の周囲環境は表面だけの観察では得られない情報を与え得る。

sentences.en: Imagine a fictional painting originally created for a narrow room in which several related works were displayed together.
sentences.ja: 関連作品が複数一緒に展示された狭い部屋用に作られた架空の絵を想像しよう。

sentences.en: When a museum later displays the painting on a large empty wall, visitors can examine details that might have been difficult to notice in its former location.
sentences.ja: 後に博物館が広い空壁に絵を展示すると来訪者は以前の場所では気づきにくかったかもしれない細部を調べられる。

sentences.en: However, they may no longer recognize how its colors or shapes were intended to relate to the objects that surrounded it.
sentences.ja: しかし色や形が周囲の物にどう関連することを意図されていたかもはや認識できないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The new arrangement provides additional opportunities for observation while removing some aspects of the original experience.
sentences.ja: 新配置は元体験の一部を取り除きながら観察の追加機会を提供する。

sentences.en: The museum staff consider displaying a diagram that indicates the approximate positions of the related works in the imagined room.
sentences.ja: 博物館職員は仮想部屋における関連作品のおおよその位置を示す図の展示を検討する。

sentences.en: They recognize that a diagram based on incomplete information could easily create a misleading impression of certainty.
sentences.ja: 不完全な情報に基づく図は確実性について誤解を招く印象を容易に作り得ると認識する。

sentences.en: Consequently, they propose distinguishing features that are supported by available records from those that have been included only to illustrate a possibility.
sentences.ja: そこで利用可能記録で支持される特徴と可能性を示すためだけに含められた特徴を区別する案を出す。

sentences.en: The example is not an account of an actual artwork or historical exhibition.
sentences.ja: 例は実作品や歴史展示の記述ではない。

sentences.en: The fictional curators also discuss how an explanation could encourage visitors to look at the painting without determining in advance exactly what each person ought to notice.
sentences.ja: 架空学芸員は各自が何に気づくべきかを事前に正確に決めず、解説が絵を見るよう促す方法も議論する。

sentences.en: Some details of a work may become more meaningful when viewers understand the purpose for which it was created.
sentences.ja: 作品の一部の細部は制作目的を鑑賞者が理解するとより意味あるものになり得る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, an exhibition can also provide opportunities for people to discover relationships that were not necessarily important to the original creator.
sentences.ja: それでも展示は当初制作者に必ずしも重要でなかった関係を人々が発見する機会も提供できる。

sentences.en: Historical context and personal interpretation do not always need to be treated as competing activities.
sentences.ja: 歴史的文脈と個人的解釈は常に競合活動と扱う必要はない。

sentences.en: A frame around a picture does more than mark the boundary of a physical object.
sentences.ja: 絵の額縁は物理的対象の境界を示す以上のことをする。

sentences.en: The wider setting in which a work is presented can also shape a viewer's understanding.
sentences.ja: 作品が提示される広い環境も鑑賞者の理解を形作り得る。

sentences.en: Recognizing those influences helps us distinguish what we encounter in an exhibition from what someone might have experienced in another place or period.
sentences.ja: その影響を認識すると展示で出会うものと別の場所・時期に誰かが体験したかもしれないものを区別できる。

sentences.en: Artistic interpretation can become richer when the relationship between these experiences is made visible.
sentences.ja: 体験間の関係が可視化されると芸術的解釈はより豊かになり得る。

vocabulary.definition: give someone a reason to act

questions.prompt: Why might the original setting matter?
options: It always makes modern exhibitions inaccurate.
It may explain aspects not apparent from the work alone.
A painting has no surface outside its original room.
Every artwork was originally displayed in a museum.
questions.explanation_ja: 元の環境から得る情報。

questions.prompt: Which factors can influence visitors' attention?
options: The cost of the museum alone.

questions.prompt: Where was the imagined painting originally created to be shown?
options: In a narrow room with related works.
questions.explanation_ja: 関連作品がある狭い部屋。

questions.prompt: What is the trade-off of the new arrangement?
options: Every original detail is necessarily lost.
The painting cannot be examined at all.
Details may be easier to see while original relationships become less apparent.
The new wall creates a completely identical experience.
A diagram showing approximate positions of related works.

questions.prompt: Why identify uncertain features in the diagram?
options: To guarantee that every illustration is historical evidence.
To prevent visitors from studying the work.
To prevent a possible reconstruction from appearing certain.
questions.explanation_ja: 確実性の誤解を避ける。

questions.prompt: Why avoid telling viewers exactly what to notice?
options: Every personal interpretation is historically correct.
Explanations should never contain useful information.
Context can inform viewing without eliminating personal discovery.

questions.prompt: What need not be treated as competing activities?
questions.explanation_ja: 歴史的文脈と個人の解釈。

options: The surroundings in which something is presented.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the passage?
options: Only the original room permits any meaningful interpretation.
Understanding art can be enriched by noticing how its setting shapes interpretation.
Modern displays always reproduce the original experience.
Historical context must eliminate personal responses.
questions.explanation_ja: 提示環境と解釈の関係。

grammar.focus: that might have been difficult to notice
grammar.explanation_ja: might have beenで過去の可能性。

grammar.focus: from those that have been included

paraphrases.source: The lighting, surrounding objects, and information provided on a label can influence the aspects of a work to which visitors pay attention.

paraphrases.source: When a museum later displays the painting on a large empty wall, visitors can examine details that might have been difficult to notice in its former location.
paraphrases.rewrite: The new location may reveal details that were harder to see before.

paraphrases.source: Consequently, they propose distinguishing features that are supported by available records from those that have been included only to illustrate a possibility.
paraphrases.rewrite: They distinguish documented features from hypothetical ones.

paraphrases.source: The fictional curators also discuss how an explanation could encourage visitors to look at the painting without determining in advance exactly what each person ought to notice.
paraphrases.rewrite: Explanations can guide observation without fixing each visitor's response.
